rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline. Five line sensors span 0.08 m across the robot's width (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m), placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so the controller reads the line before the wheels reach it. Weights are set to the sensor x-positions scaled to -2..+2, so the steering signal is roughly proportional to the line's lateral offset, with positive (left) steering when the tape sits on the left sensors. Gains: kp = 2.0 gives a full-scale signal of about 700 PWM of wheel differential, which is firm without being aggressive. ki is small (0.05) to avoid integral windup on curves, and kd = 0.2 damps oscillation. base_speed = 1.6 (about 78% PWM) aims for the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving headroom for turns. line_loss = last_direction lets the robot recover toward the side it last saw the line. Geometry is mid-range (wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.12 x 0.16 m), with the body width giving a comfortable off-track margin. Expected result: the robot completes the oval and s-bend with low rms error and few line losses. The main risk is oscillation at 1.6 speed on the slalom, which the steering_oscillation measurement should reveal. Hypotheses to test next: (1) if oscillation is high, reduce kp or raise kd; (2) if the robot drifts wide on bends, raise kp or base_speed-appropriate gain; (3) if completion_time is over 3 s with completion, raise base_speed.
